findings.label: The supporting production
findings.title: Keep the running-back improvement. Criticize the rest.
findings.body: Cody improves his running-back production, and the flex spots give back even more. Chase Brown and Kaelon Black supplied 18.2, up from last week’s 7.6; the flex fell from 30.3 to 11.4. Sandy won by 30.10. No, improving the running backs did not fix the team. We can criticize the rest without requiring Cody to have done nothing right.

findings.label: The active allocation
findings.title: First name the player who comes out.
findings.body: Bennett used both flex positions on running backs. Along with the two RB slots, that put Williams, Gibbs, Irving and Jacobs to work for 77 points. Tucker’s 20.8 remained on the bench. I am happy to consider an alternative; first name who leaves the lineup. A conspicuous reserve score is not free extra production.

findings.label: The changed consequence
findings.title: The tight-end gap shrank. It did not change sides.
findings.body: T. Ocellus won, but the tight-end evidence has not switched sides. Pitts outscored Higbee again. The unused gap fell from 18.3 to 8.3; it did not become negative. Bryan’s 28.26-point victory gives the comparison rather more comfortable surroundings. I see no reason to remove it.

findings.label: The small available improvement
findings.title: Corey could not use Patrick’s bench.
findings.body: Bo Nix and Tony Pollard left 67.28 unused for Patrick. Interesting, but Corey could not spend any of it. His own Addison-for-Coker improvement was 1.9, and that was enough. Last week Corey’s second-highest score ran into DOGE’s highest. This time the winning hindsight swap was on his own roster. No transaction with Patrick required.

findings.label: The unfilled position
findings.title: The occupied places deserve a mention.
findings.body: Moe’s unfilled kicker slot has the advantage of being easy to notice. KC Concepcion and CeeDee Lamb deserve some of that attention: 41.1 between them in a 26.46-point win. Even Andrew’s better flex swap leaves 18.76 to find. The empty place may be mentioned. It need not be made the guest of honor.

findings.label: The unglamorous separation
findings.title: Four receivers, all below nine.
findings.body: Four receivers give a lineup a certain air of extravagance. Pete got fewer than nine from each. Ordway’s Drake Maye and Will Reichard outscored Pete’s quarterback-kicker pair by 26.42, most of a 34.32-point win. I realize the kicker is not usually the aspirational purchase. Neither is four separate versions of the same disappointing afternoon.
